variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Bara Kitchen revised character wardrobe / preset sheet.
The user likes the existing character QUALITY and FACE. Preserve the source animal's exact species identity, facial shapes, fur colors/markings, head/body ratio, tiny connected legs, small bare paws and feet, simple black oval animal eyes, and soft rounded 3D rendering. Edit wardrobe, accessories and composition only. Do not replace the face, lengthen the muzzle, add human fingers, make the body taller/thinner, or give female characters human anatomy, human hair, makeup or long eyelashes. LAYOUT CHANGE IS ESSENTIAL: produce exactly FOUR full-body depictions of the SAME species in a spacious 2x2 SQUARE concept sheet, roughly 2048x2048. All four face slightly toward camera in a front three-quarter view so their whole outfit and both eyes can be assessed. Top left MALE CHEF, top right FEMALE CHEF, bottom left MALE CUSTOMER, bottom right FEMALE CUSTOMER. Every figure is equally sized from feet to skull crown, hats/ears extend above that. Clear dark-brown sans-serif labels above each quadrant, exact text: "MALE CHEF", "FEMALE CHEF", "MALE CUSTOMER", "FEMALE CUSTOMER". No other text or props. Exactly four characters, no fifth figure and no side-profile-only customer.
READABILITY: decorations must be OBVIOUS. Each character gets a substantial recognizable head accessory. Female bows should span approximately 25–30% of head width, have broad ribbon loops, and have a contrasting ivory/dark edge; never a tiny flower or a fur-colored clip. Keep ears visible around hats/headbands. Male characters must also have prominent decorations, not an undecorated default. Retain the same friendly animal eyes and underlying body for both presets. Distinguish presets through hat silhouette, collar/neckwear and clothing cut, not just color.
CHEFS: retain the ivory café chef family but visibly differentiate the two uniforms. Female chef: a lower rounded ivory fabric chef cap with a wide colored band and a LARGE contrasting bow at one side, ivory blouse with rounded collar, colored short bib apron with broad straps and one large ivory pocket, cocoa undershorts. CUSTOMERS: absolutely no chef hats or aprons; use the individual outfits below. Their outfits must differ in SHAPE as well as color. Short hems preserve tiny legs and visible animal feet. Do not copy the old identical sage vest outfit.

MALE CUSTOMER: Cream rolled-sleeve shirt, navy suspenders over cocoa shorts, a large mustard bow tie, and a navy newsboy cap with an ivory band.
FEMALE CUSTOMER: Ivory blouse with rounded collar under a deep-plum short pinafore with two large cream pockets. Wide ivory headband with a very large plum bow edged in ivory. Brown undershorts and tiny bare capybara feet.
Keep the source Capybara head shape, eyes, muzzle and species ears/tail consistent in all FOUR views. All four bodies stay very short and cute.
